extracted.intended_audience: judges, policymakers, court administrators, and IP practitioners involved with the Patent Court (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative metrics for improving the Patent Court's decision quality, internationalization, specialization, jurisdictional scope, and operational performance (including statistical indicators). Targets reform and performance measurement of a national patent court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhancement of hearing and excellence of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancement of hearing and excellence of decisions are the most important tasks upon the Patent Court; all members of the Patent Court including judges need to devote their efforts and research to this end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges and court members should devote sustained effort and research to improve hearings and decision quality; use of expert witnesses and appraisals is indicated as part of achieving excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internationalization and specialization of Patent Court
rubrics_metrics.description: With the enforcement of amendments, the Patent Court must establish and operate an International Division to promote expertise and excellence to the international community by carrying out dedicated hearing and rendering quality decisions on international cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish foundation for the International Division; handle international cases with dedicated hearing procedures and high-quality decisions; account for the fact that roughly 30% of cases involve a foreign party; decisions should serve as international references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote competence, professionalism and fairness of judges and judicial technical examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority and reliability of decisions, especially in international cases, depend on the competence, professionalism and fairness of the judges and judicial technical examiners who assist trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously promote measures and efforts to strengthen internationalization and specialization of judges and technical examiners (training, recruitment, specialization policies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation and dissemination of decisions for international use
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on international cases should be translated into foreign languages and used as reference for litigation and research in other countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate important decisions and disseminate them internationally to enhance the court's reputation and to provide authoritative references for foreign litigants and scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish practice direction early and improve guidelines for civil infringement suits
rubrics_metrics.description: As civil infringement suits are under the exclusive jurisdiction of the Patent Court, infringement hearings and trials call for early establishment of the court’s practice direction and improvement of existing guidelines considering the unique and specialized nature of IP disputes and their efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and publish practice directions and refine guidelines tailored to IP disputes to ensure consistent and efficient adjudication of infringement cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop procedures to include appeals from interim motions (e.g., preliminary injunctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures must be developed so that the court’s exclusive jurisdiction would include appeals from motions such as preliminary injunctions, allowing the court to hear and adjudicate main claims and motions promptly and consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue procedural reforms (and where needed, legislative changes) to ensure the Patent Court can decide both main claims and significant interlocutory motions in a cohesive, time-efficient manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue legislation to amend trial levels and jurisdiction to cover criminal and other related cases
rubrics_metrics.description: In the long term, legislation should be pursued to ensure first-instance trials and appeals in criminal cases related to patent and other rights, revocation of administrative decision, and civil appeals are adjudicated by the Patent Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider expanding statutory jurisdiction and adjusting trial levels so the Patent Court adjudicates a wider set of IP-related matters (criminal, administrative revocation, civil appeals) to centralize expertise and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand exclusive jurisdiction of a specialized court to resolve IP disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive jurisdiction of a specialized court (the Patent Court) is needed to resolve IP disputes to mitigate inconsistency/unreasonableness in decisions, litigation delays, cost waste from jurisdictional separation, and delays in industrial development due to insufficient protection at an early stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizing IP dispute resolution in a specialized court is framed as foundational for the Patent Court to become the central and most advanced national and international IP court over the next 10–20 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case-volume statistics as performance indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Track annual numbers of cases filed, handled, unresolved, and appealed (including rates of change and appeal rates) as core metrics of court activity and workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables (e.g., Table 1) present these as primary indicators; percentages are explained as year-over-year rate of change and appeal rates as appeals out of all decisions. Use these metrics to monitor trends and resource needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor case-type breakdowns (patent, utility model, design, trademark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and compare filings, handled cases, unresolved counts and appeal rates separately by case type (patent, utility model, design, trademark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables 2–6 give detailed annual stats by case type; monitoring each category supports targeted policy and resource allocation for differing workloads and complexities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track inter partes versus ex parte case ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the proportion of inter partes and ex parte cases among filings for each case type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 2 provides inter partes/ex parte percentages; these ratios inform procedural planning because inter partes cases often have different evidentiary and scheduling needs than ex parte matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure administrative trial and IPTAB decision volumes and dispositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Count administrative trial (IPTAB) decisions by category and track litigated and revoked outcomes, with percentages of litigated and revoked decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables 7-1 and 7-2 show total IPTAB decisions and the share that are litigated or revoked; definitions and percentages are provided for interpreting these administrative-adjudicative outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track litigated and revoked administrative decisions (definitions and ratios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor the proportion of administrative trial decisions that are litigated and the proportion of decisions that resulted in revocation (full revocation excluding partial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table notes define 'litigated' as suits against administrative trial decisions and 'revoked' as decisions revoking all of the administrative trial decision (excluding partial revocation); use these ratios to assess administrative decision robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure processing-time distributions and averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Record distribution of case processing periods (within 6 months; 6 months to less than 1 year; 1 to 2 years; more than 2 years) and average processing period (in days) by case type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables 8-1 and 8-2 and Figure 6 present processing-time buckets and average days; these metrics are key for assessing timeliness, efficiency, and identifying delay drivers by case type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure cross-border case activity and country breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Count cross-border cases and the number of involved foreigners (including corporations) by country, and calculate the percentage of cross-border cases out of total cases handled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 9 breaks down foreign involvement (e.g., US, Japan, EU countries) and percentage share of cross-border cases; these data support internationalization planning and resource allocation for international litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track civil appeals processing and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor civil appeals: numbers filed and handled, unresolved counts, disposition breakdowns (decision/mediation/others), appeals to the Supreme Court, and processing-time categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables 10–11 summarize civil appeals statistics and processing times; use them to measure appellate workload and time-to-resolution for civil IP matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'Others' in 'number of cases handled' as withdrawn/closed categories
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Others' in the 'number of cases handled' refers to cases withdrawn, deemed withdrawn, or closed with an order to dismiss the complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This classification note (table footnote) clarifies what non-decision dispositions are included in handled-case totals; necessary for accurate interpretation of handling statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define percentage calculations and appeal-rate metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage (%) in 'filed, handled and unresolved' is the rate of increase/decrease compared with the previous year; percentage (%) in 'appeal' is the rate of appeals out of all decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table footnotes explicitly define how percentage metrics are computed—use these definitions when comparing year-over-year statistics or calculating appeal intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document major decisions and legal holdings as reference for practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix includes summaries of major Patent Court decisions (e.g., standing of non-exclusive licensee to file invalidation action) with main issues and holdings and summary of decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and publish key precedents and summaries (two decades of major decisions) to guide judges, practitioners, and to support consistent application of law across cases.
